question: Is the train-min F1 floor the same minority classes on every fold, or different ones?
method: Compare observed train_min macro-F1 to majority-only theoretical macro-F1 over present classes (predict all-majority). Per-class F1 not in fold stamps (no saved logits); majority-only equivalence identifies the failure mode without a replay.

salt_hydrophobe_absent_from_labels.implication: M2 macro-F1 never includes salt/hydrophobe — they cannot be the floor-sitters on this card. Same R0/R1 argmax geometry as A-r5-lever / L-argmax-dominated-by-r0-r1.

train_min_equals_majority_only_classifie.read: On every fold, the worst train structure's macro-F1 equals (to float noise) the theoretical majority-only macro-F1 over {0,1,4} ≈ 1/3. Model predicts all-NEIGHBORHOOD on that structure: F1(4)≈1, F1(0)=F1(1)=0 → macro≈0.32.

which_classes_floor.answer: SAME on every fold: CORE (0) and DEHYDRON_RIM (1) sit at F1=0 under all-maj prediction; NEIGHBORHOOD (4) is the majority basin.
which_classes_floor.not_salt_hydrophobe: Salt/hydrophobe are not in the metric at all.
which_classes_floor.not_structure_varying_rare_class: Victims of train-min rotate (1IVO 5/12, 4OBE 3/12, 2SHP 2/12, …) but the class pattern is identical everywhere.

vs_typed_path.shared_upstream: R0/R1-dominated argmax produces empty salt/hydrophobe labels AND NEIGHBORHOOD majority — construction-level link.
vs_typed_path.distinct_failure_here: M2 min miss is majority-CE collapse on the two present minorities (CORE, DEHYDRON_RIM), which do have labels. A-typed-path is about rel_bias/gamma/beta gradient silence when typed edges exist — complementary, not identical.
vs_typed_path.agenda_language: Confirms persistent majority-basin fit failure on CORE+DEHYDRON_RIM under this stack — not proof that typed-path silence is the bottleneck for M2, and not a generic 'random rare class per fold' story.

heldout_note: Most held folds also sit within ~0.01 of maj-only floor; a few slightly above (1BG1 Δ+0.029, 1F88 +0.021) without clearing 0.40.
